attachment.content:
- verify-all: Run the full check + clippy sweep across the workspace AND the WASM plugin (panopt-zellij). Use after non-trivial edits, before declaring work done, or when asked to verify the repo builds cleanly. Captures the dual-target dance (workspace builds for host, panopt-zellij builds only for wasm32-wasip1) so you don't have to remember the right manifest-path/target each time.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

{"id":135,"title":"EPIC: Agent model — types (profiles) → configs (slots) → instances (runs)","body":"Umbrella for refining the agent model into three explicit levels, converged in design discussion 2026-05-31. Tracks the child todos tagged `agent-model`.

## The three levels

1. **Agent types = data (profiles), not code.** A type is a *profile row* that drives a fixed set of generic interpreters; `tool_type` becomes a key into a profile registry. There is no per-type code in the common case.
   - **Launch is data**: a spawn-spec template — `argv` template + `env` map + `files`-to-materialize — over a fixed placeholder set (`{agent_id, name, token, mcp_url, project_path, cwd, model, …}`). env-vs-flag-vs-config-file are just *where a placeholder lands*, not different mechanisms. One substitution engine, not a branch per type.
   - **Status is data**: pattern rules (`thinking/idle/waiting/done`) over agent output, run by one generic pattern engine.
   - **Irreducibly code** (fixed, generic, never per-type): the interpreters (substitution, pattern, health/pane-death) and the placeholder providers (the code that produces `token`/`mcp_url`/`agent_id`). New per-type code is needed only for a genuinely new *step kind* the interpreters can't express — rare, and reusable as data once added.
   - **Scope**: global, layered — shipped-defaults file ← machine/user overrides. Distinct from per-project `agent_tools`.

2. **Agent configs = per-project durable slots** (`agent_tools`, shipped in #27). Reference a type; hold name, cwd, command/arg overrides, system prompt, `enabled`. A slot is a lifecycle-managed line in the project's agents pane.

3. **Agent instances = per-project ephemeral runs** (`processes`, shipped in #27 with reserved `pid/status/agent_state/last_seen`). Reference a config; one per config (1:1 policy, N:1 door left open). Born on start, die on stop.

## Why config and instance stay separate even at 1:1
They are *desired state vs. running state* (spec/status): config = what you want, instance = what's happening, and they legitimately diverge (edited-but-not-restarted, crashed, never-started). Decisively, run-level identity is needed so **sessions (#113) and plans (#105) attach to a run, not the durable slot**. The 1:1 keeps the *UI* one-row-per-slot regardless.

## Relationship to existing todos
- #27 (config/instance schema split) — **schema + MCP surface shipped**; remaining wiring lives in the `tool_type → profile` child. Recommend verifying and closing #27.
- #83 (declared-identity registry) — the registry is the *runtime presence* of an instance; the liveness child must consume it, not re-model liveness.
- #111 (monitor agent status in pane) — **absorbed** by the lifecycle-UI child.
- #105 (plans), #113 (sessions) — downstream consumers; this work gives them a run to attach to.

## Agent orchestration surface (solo parity) — added 2026-06-06
The model + lifecycle + human-cockpit-UI children leave a gap: the **agent-facing orchestration surface** an orchestrator agent uses to spawn + bootstrap + task + dispose sub-agents (modelled on solo's `spawn_agent`/`send_input`/`close_process`). Two new children, both riding the #141 daemon-decides / plugin-effects seam:
- **#159 — spawn surface**: `spawn_agent` alias over `process_start`; returns rendered `agent_instructions` (per-type profile template, #136/#137); per-launch `name`/`extra_args` that don't mutate the config.
- **#160 — input channel**: `send_input(process_id, input)` enqueued by the daemon, written into the owned pane by the plugin (`write_chars_to_pane_id`). The linchpin that turns a spawned child into a working one with no human keystroke.

Mappings & non-goals:
- solo's `close_process` == panopt's existing `process_stop` (kill process, **pane stands** per the never-close-panes invariant) + `process_delete`. No new tool needed; documented on #141.
- `project_id` cross-project spawn is a **deferred non-goal** — collides with the per-connection `?ws=` project scoping. Revisit when a real cross-project orchestration case appears.

## DESIGN
Split §6.6 into configs/instances + a new §6.7 "Agent type profiles"; promote §10's spawn bullet into a real lifecycle subsection. 1	//! `panopt` - the PANopt cockpit launcher.
2	//!
3	//! Brings up the coordination daemon on demand and the Zellij cockpit, and
4	//! opens agent panes - each with a stable per-agent identity (DESIGN.md §9).
5

36	#[derive(Parser)]
37	#[command(name = "panopt", about = "PANopt cockpit launcher", version)]
38	struct Cli {
39	    /// Port the panopt daemon listens on.
40	    #[arg(long, default_value_t = 7600, global = true)]
41	    port: u16,
42	
43	    #[command(subcommand)]
44	    command: Cmd,
45	}
46	
47	#[derive(Subcommand)]
48	enum Cmd {
49	    /// Boot the cockpit: the daemon, a Zellij session, the sidebar, and an
50	    /// agent. Attaches if the cockpit is already running.
51	    Up {
52	        /// Path to the panopt-zellij plugin `.wasm` (auto-detected from a dev
53	        /// build when omitted).
54	        #[arg(long)]
55	        plugin: Option<PathBuf>,
56	        /// Bind address for the daemon when this call starts it. Defaults to
57	        /// `127.0.0.1`; pass `0.0.0.0` to accept connections from agents on
58	        /// other machines (the bearer-token gate still applies). Ignored if
59	        /// the daemon is already running.
60	        #[arg(long)]
61	        host: Option<String>,
62	    },
63	    /// Open a new agent pane in the running cockpit.
64	    Agent {
65	        /// Optional readable name for the agent.
66	        name: Option<String>,
67	    },
68	    /// Print a `--mcp-config` JSON for a hand-launched Claude Code session.
69	    ///
70	    /// The emitted config gives the session a stable agent id, a friendly
71	    /// display name, and the bearer token, so a manually started agent is
72	    /// indistinguishable from a cockpit-spawned one in the coordination plane.
73	    ///
74	    /// Example:
75	    ///   claude --mcp-config "$(panopt agent-config --name greg-main)"
76	    #[command(name = "agent-config")]
77	    AgentConfig {
78	        /// Friendly display name shown to other agents (default: the id).
79	        #[arg(long)]
80	        name: Option<String>,
81	        /// Stable agent id put on the MCP URL (default: $USER-$HOSTNAME).
82	        #[arg(long)]
83	        id: Option<String>,
84	        /// Daemon host (default: 127.0.0.1).
85	        #[arg(long)]
86	        host: Option<String>,
87	        /// Bearer token for the daemon's auth gate (default: read from
88	        /// `~/.local/share/panopt/token`). Pass inline when configuring an
89	        /// agent on another machine - get the value from the daemon host
90	        /// with `panopt token`.
91	        #[arg(long)]
92	        token: Option<String>,
93	        /// Project root (default: the current directory).
94	        #[arg(long)]
95	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
96	    },
97	    /// Manage this project's committed identity (`.panopt/project-id`), the
98	    /// stable repo key PANopt prefers over the checkout path.
99	    Project {
100	        /// Project root (default: the current directory).
101	        #[arg(long, global = true)]
102	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
103	        #[command(subcommand)]
104	        action: project::ProjectCmd,
105	    },
106	    /// Print the daemon's bearer token to stdout.
107	    ///
108	    /// Useful when configuring an agent on another machine: read the token
109	    /// from the daemon host (e.g. `ssh nixos panopt token`) and pass it to
110	    /// `panopt agent-config --token <value>` on the agent host, which then
111	    /// does not need a local token file.
112	    Token,
113	    /// Inspect and edit the project's shared todos.
114	    Todo {
115	        /// Project root the todos belong to (default: the current directory).
116	        #[arg(long, global = true)]
117	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
118	        #[command(subcommand)]
119	        action: todo::TodoCmd,
120	    },
121	    /// Inspect and edit the project's agent tools (durable spawn configs).
122	    #[command(name = "agent-tool")]
123	    AgentTool {
124	        /// Project root the agent tools belong to (default: the current directory).
125	        #[arg(long, global = true)]
126	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
127	        #[command(subcommand)]
128	        action: agent_tool::AgentToolCmd,
129	    },
130	    /// Inspect and edit the project's processes (agent/command/terminal instances).
131	    Process {
132	        /// Project root the processes belong to (default: the current directory).
133	        #[arg(long, global = true)]
134	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
135	        #[command(subcommand)]
136	        action: process::ProcessCmd,
137	    },
138	    /// Operate on the project's notes from the CLI. Currently exposes
139	    /// only `rm`; the rest of the surface lives in the cockpit's editor form.
140	    Note {
141	        /// Project root the notes belong to (default: the current directory).
142	        #[arg(long, global = true)]
143	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
144	        #[command(subcommand)]
145	        action: note::NoteCmd,
146	    },
147	    /// Popup search across the project's todos and notes. Intended for
148	    /// the cockpit (the sidebar plugin spawns this in a floating pane via the
149	    /// search keybind), but also runs standalone — Enter prints `kind:id` to
150	    /// stdout when not under Zellij.
151	    Search {
152	        /// Project root to search (default: the current directory).
153	        #[arg(long)]
154	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
155	    },
156	    /// Resolve a numeric id to its resource kind (todo / note /
157	    /// agent-tool / process) via the daemon's `id_kind` MCP tool.
158	    #[command(name = "id-kind")]
159	    IdKind {
160	        /// Project root the id belongs to (default: the current directory).
161	        #[arg(long)]
162	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
163	        /// Numeric id to resolve.
164	        id: u64,
165	    },
166	    /// Internal: the entrypoint that runs inside an agent pane.
167	    #[command(name = "_agent", hide = true)]
168	    AgentExec {
169	        #[arg(long)]
170	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
171	        #[arg(long)]
172	        id: Option<String>,
173	    },
174	    /// Internal: call `agent_leave` on the daemon as `id`, so its registry
175	    /// entry and advisory locks clear immediately. Used by the plugin's
176	    /// pane-death hook to tear down a cockpit-spawned agent the moment its
177	    /// pane closes, without waiting for the idle sweep.
178	    #[command(name = "_agent-leave", hide = true)]
179	    AgentLeave {
180	        #[arg(long)]
181	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
182	        /// Stable agent id (the `?agent=` value the dead pane connected with).
183	        #[arg(long)]
184	        id: String,
185	    },
186	    /// Internal: long-lived stdio MCP server that forwards to panoptd over
187	    /// HTTP. Claude Code spawns this via `--mcp-config` so its connection
188	    /// stays up across panoptd restarts.
189	    #[command(name = "_mcp-proxy", hide = true)]
190	    McpProxy {
191	        /// Daemon host (default: 127.0.0.1).
192	        #[arg(long, default_value = "127.0.0.1")]
193	        host: String,
194	        /// Project root the agent is scoped to.
195	        #[arg(long)]
196	        ws: PathBuf,
197	        /// Opaque project identity key (becomes `?project=` on the panoptd URL).
198	        /// Defaults to deriving it from `ws`: committed `.panopt/project-id` ->
199	        /// remote URL -> root commit -> path.
200	        #[arg(long)]
201	        project: Option<String>,
202	        /// Stable agent id (becomes `?agent=` on the panoptd URL).
203	        #[arg(long)]
204	        id: String,
205	        /// Friendly display name (becomes `?name=` on the panoptd URL).
206	        #[arg(long)]
207	        name: String,
208	        /// Bearer token for the daemon's auth gate.
209	        #[arg(long)]
210	        token: String,
211	    },
212	    /// Internal: start a process in this pane.
213	    #[command(name = "_process-run", hide = true)]
214	    ProcessRun {
215	        #[arg(long)]
216	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
217	        /// Numeric id of the process to start.
218	        id: u64,
219	    },
220	    /// Internal: report runtime facts for a reconciled instance - the pane it
221	    /// landed in (once, at reconcile) and/or its latest classified activity
222	    /// (each poll the state changes, todo #142). Both are optional so the two
223	    /// reporters call independently.
224	    #[command(name = "_process-report", hide = true)]
225	    ProcessReport {
226	        #[arg(long)]
227	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
228	        /// Numeric id of the process being reported on.
229	        #[arg(long)]
230	        id: u64,
231	        /// Opaque pane identifier (the Zellij terminal id) to record.
232	        #[arg(long = "pane-id")]
233	        pane_id: Option<String>,
234	        /// Classified activity (`thinking`/`idle`/`waiting`/`done`) to record.
235	        #[arg(long = "agent-state")]
236	        agent_state: Option<String>,
237	    },
238	    /// Internal: a long-lived cockpit viewer pane.
239	    #[command(name = "_viewer", hide = true)]
240	    ViewerExec {
241	        #[arg(long)]
242	        ws: Option<PathBuf>,
243	        /// Routing-file token the sidebar plugin assigned this pane.
244	        #[arg(long)]
245	        slot: String,
246	        /// Initial item kind: todo, note, todo-list, note-list.
247	        #[arg(long)]
248	        kind: Option<String>,
249	        /// Initial item id, for the todo and note kinds.
250	        #[arg(long)]
251	        id: Option<u64>,
252	    },
253	    /// Internal: the floating close-gate dialog the sidebar plugin spawns
254	    /// when a destructive action would lose active items.
255	    #[command(name = "_close-gate", hide = true)]
256	    CloseGateExec {
257	        /// What the user tried to do: focus, tab, or quit.
258	        #[arg(long)]
259	        scope: String,
260	        /// Active items the dialog shows: `kind:label;kind:label;...`.
261	        #[arg(long, default_value = "")]
262	        items: String,
263	        /// Terminal pane id to close when scope is `focus`.
264	        #[arg(long)]
265	        target_pane: Option<u32>,
266	    },
267	    /// Internal: the floating delete-confirmation dialog the sidebar plugin
268	    /// spawns when the user presses `x` on a row.
269	    #[command(name = "_delete-gate", hide = true)]
270	    DeleteGateExec {
271	        /// Item kind: todo, note, agent-tool, or process.
272	        #[arg(long)]
273	        kind: String,
274	        /// Numeric id of the item the user wants to delete.
275	        #[arg(long)]
276	        id: u64,
277	        /// Human label for the row (title / name); shown in the dialog.
278	        #[arg(long, default_value = "")]
279	        label: String,
280	    },
281	}
282	
283	fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
284	    let cli = Cli::parse();
285	    match cli.command {
286	        Cmd::Up { plugin, host } => up::run(plugin, host, cli.port),
287	        Cmd::Agent { name } => agent::spawn(name),
288	        Cmd::AgentConfig {
289	            name,
290	            id,
291	            host,
292	            token,
293	            ws,
294	        } => agent_config::run(host, cli.port, id, name, token, ws),
295	        Cmd::Project { ws, action } => project::run(ws, action),
296	        Cmd::Token => {
297	            use anyhow::Context;
298	            let token = panopt_core::auth::read_token(&paths::token()?)
299	                .context("reading the panopt token (start the daemon with `panopt up`)")?;
300	            println!("{token}");
301	            Ok(())
302	        }
303	        Cmd::Todo { ws, action } => todo::run(ws, action, cli.port),
304	        Cmd::AgentTool { ws, action } => agent_tool::run(ws, action, cli.port),
305	        Cmd::Process { ws, action } => process::run(ws, action, cli.port),
306	        Cmd::Note { ws, action } => note::run(ws, action, cli.port),
307	        Cmd::Search { ws } => search::run(ws, cli.port),
308	        Cmd::IdKind { ws, id } => id_kind::run(ws, id, cli.port),
309	        Cmd::AgentExec { ws, id } => agent::exec_in_pane(ws, id, cli.port),
310	        Cmd::AgentLeave { ws, id } => agent::leave(ws, id, cli.port),
311	        Cmd::McpProxy {
312	            host,
313	            ws,
314	            project,
315	            id,
316	            name,
317	            token,
318	        } => mcp_proxy::run(host, cli.port, ws, project, id, name, token),
319	        Cmd::ProcessRun { ws, id } => process::exec_entry(ws, id, cli.port),
320	        Cmd::ProcessReport {
321	            ws,
322	            id,
323	            pane_id,
324	            agent_state,
325	        } => process::exec_report(ws, id, pane_id, agent_state, cli.port),
326	        Cmd::ViewerExec { ws, slot, kind, id } => viewer::run(ws, cli.port, slot, kind, id),
327	        Cmd::CloseGateExec {
328	            scope,
329	            items,
330	            target_pane,
331	        } => close_gate::run(&scope, &items, target_pane, cli.port),
332	        Cmd::DeleteGateExec { kind, id, label } => delete_gate::run(&kind, id, &label, cli.port),
333	    }
334	}

1	//! `panopt _viewer` - a long-lived cockpit content pane.
2	//!
3	//! Renders one item from the project's `.panopt/` projection - a list of
4	//! items - or, for the todo and note kinds, hosts the matching shared
5	//! editable form ([`crate::todo_form`] / [`crate::note_form`]). The
6	//! sidebar plugin re-points the pane at a different item by writing a routing
7	//! file the viewer polls; switching item saves the outgoing item's scroll
8	//! position and restores the incoming one's (see [`crate::viewstate`]).
9	//!
10	//! Index views come from the projected `.panopt/*.md` files, which the daemon
11	//! keeps current. Todos and notes are special: the viewer opens an MCP
12	//! session and renders the matching form against live `todo_get` /
13	//! `note_get` data, autosaving on a debounce. The pane is long-lived:
14	//! it closes only when the user presses Ctrl-C, never on its own.
15	
16	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
17	use std::time::{Duration, Instant, SystemTime};
18	
19	use std::io::stdout;
20	
21	use anyhow::{Context, Result};
22	use crossterm::event::{
23	    self, DisableBracketedPaste, DisableMouseCapture, EnableBracketedPaste, EnableMouseCapture,
24	    Event, KeyCode, KeyEvent, KeyEventKind, KeyModifiers, MouseButton, MouseEvent, MouseEventKind,
25	};
26	use crossterm::execute;
27	use ratatui::layout::{Constraint, Layout, Rect};
28	use ratatui::style::{Color, Modifier, Style};
29	use ratatui::text::{Line, Text};
30	use ratatui::widgets::{Paragraph, Wrap};
31	use ratatui::{DefaultTerminal, Frame};
32	use serde_json::{json, Value};
33	
34	use crate::mcpclient::Client;
35	use crate::note_form::NoteForm;
36	use crate::todo::observer_url;
37	use crate::todo_form::TodoForm;
38	use crate::viewstate::{self, ViewState};
39	
40	/// File the cockpit's Todos gatekeeper publishes the live right-side pane
41	/// count to (under the project's `.panopt/.cockpit/`). A `_viewer` reads it to
42	/// learn whether it is the only content pane left - the one it must not close,
43	/// since closing it makes Zellij re-tile and the five plugin panes stop being
44	/// a sidebar. Outside the cockpit the file is absent and viewers stay closable.
45	/// See [`Viewer::close_gesture`].
46	const CONTENT_COUNT_FILE: &str = "content-count";
47	
48	/// How often the viewer wakes to poll the routing file and refresh content.
49	const TICK: Duration = Duration::from_millis(250);
50	/// The shortest gap between re-reads of the displayed content file.
51	const REFRESH: Duration = Duration::from_millis(800);
52	/// How long an unsaved scalar-field edit waits before the viewer flushes it.
53	const DEBOUNCE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(300);
54	
55	/// What a viewer pane is currently showing.
56	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
57	enum Target {
58	    Todo(u64),
59	    /// A brand-new todo, not yet persisted. The form sends `todo_create` on
60	    /// the first autosave with a non-empty title; from then on it behaves
61	    /// like a `Todo(id)`.
62	    NewTodo,
63	    Note(u64),
64	    /// A brand-new note, not yet persisted. The form sends
65	    /// `note_create` on the first autosave with a non-empty title; from
66	    /// then on it behaves like a `Note(id)`.
67	    NewNote,
68	    TodoList,
69	    NoteList,
70	    Empty,
71	}
72	
73	impl Target {
74	    /// Parse a routing payload's `kind`/`id` pair into a target. The `empty`
75	    /// kind lets the sidebar clear the viewer when nothing is selected; the
76	    /// `new-todo` / `new-note` kinds open blank forms.
77	    fn parse(kind: &str, id: Option<u64>) -> Option<Target> {
78	        match (kind, id) {
79	            ("todo", Some(id)) => Some(Target::Todo(id)),

221	    /// on an unrecognised value (a forward-compatibility hedge for stored
222	    /// filters whose meaning has since shifted).
223	    fn parse(s: &str) -> TodoFilter {

226	            .copied()

231	    /// Next filter in the cycle, wrapping at the end.

238	    fn prev(self) -> TodoFilter {
239	        let i = ALL_FILTERS.iter().position(|f| *f == self).unwrap_or(0);

248	            return true;

251	            TodoFilter::All => true,
252	            TodoFilter::Open => status == "open",
253	            TodoFilter::Active => {
254	                (status == "open" && !entry.is_blocked) || status == "in_progress"
255	            }
256	            TodoFilter::InProgress => status == "in_progress",
257	            TodoFilter::Backlog => status == "backlog",
258	            TodoFilter::Draft => status == "draft",
259	            TodoFilter::Completed => status == "completed",
260	            TodoFilter::NotDone => status == "not_done",
261	        }

278	/// One axis of the two-level todo sort. The list view carries two of these
279	/// (level 1 / level 2) and applies them as a stable two-pass sort, so equal
280	/// keys on level 1 are broken by level 2. Each axis maps a [`ListEntry`] to
281	/// an `Ordering` via [`Self::cmp_entries`].
282	///
283	/// `PriorityDesc` is the only priority axis - low → high is rarely useful.
284	/// Created and modified date each get both directions because either makes
285	/// sense depending on what the user is hunting for (newest activity vs.
286	/// oldest unfinished).
287	/// Level 1's default is `PriorityDesc`; level 2 defaults to
288	/// [`TodoSort::CreatedAsc`] in [`Viewer::new`] - the two levels have
289	/// different defaults, so the `Default` value alone doesn't tell the whole
290	/// story.
291	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
292	enum TodoSort {
293	    #[default]
294	    PriorityDesc,
295	    CreatedAsc,
296	    CreatedDesc,
297	    ModifiedAsc,
298	    ModifiedDesc,
299	}

301	impl TodoSort {
302	    /// Display label. `/` indicates ascending (low → high), `\` indicates
303	    /// descending (high → low); priority is single-direction (high → low)
304	    /// so it carries no suffix. Also the viewstate-stored token via
305	    /// [`Self::as_key`] - the display form doubles as the persistence
306	    /// form, so a label tweak invalidates any persisted prefs and falls
307	    /// back to the default through [`Self::parse`].
308	    fn label(self) -> &'static str {
309	        match self {
310	            TodoSort::PriorityDesc => "priority",
311	            TodoSort::CreatedAsc => "created-/",
312	            TodoSort::CreatedDesc => "created-\\",
313	            TodoSort::ModifiedAsc => "modified-/",
314	            TodoSort::ModifiedDesc => "modified-\\",
315	        }
316	    }
317	
318	    /// The serialised form used by viewstate, identical to [`Self::label`].
319	    fn as_key(self) -> &'static str {
320	        self.label()
321	    }
322	
323	    /// Parse a viewstate-stored token, defaulting to [`TodoSort::default`]
324	    /// on an unrecognised value.
325	    fn parse(s: &str) -> TodoSort {
326	        ALL_SORTS
327	            .iter()
328	            .copied()
329	            .find(|x| x.as_key() == s)
330	            .unwrap_or_default()
331	    }
332	
333	    /// Next sort in the cycle, wrapping at the end.
334	    fn next(self) -> TodoSort {
335	        let i = ALL_SORTS.iter().position(|x| *x == self).unwrap_or(0);
336	        ALL_SORTS[(i + 1) % ALL_SORTS.len()]
337	    }
338	
339	    /// Previous sort in the cycle, wrapping at the start.
340	    fn prev(self) -> TodoSort {
341	        let i = ALL_SORTS.iter().position(|x| *x == self).unwrap_or(0);
342	        ALL_SORTS[(i + ALL_SORTS.len() - 1) % ALL_SORTS.len()]
343	    }
344	
345	    /// Compare two entries on this axis. Entries that lack the field this
346	    /// axis reads sort after entries that have it (so missing data lands at
347	    /// the end of the list rather than mixed in).
348	    fn cmp_entries(self, a: &ListEntry, b: &ListEntry) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
349	        match self {
350	            TodoSort::PriorityDesc => {
351	                let rank = |p: &Option<String>| match p.as_deref() {
352	                    Some("high") => 3,
353	                    Some("medium") => 2,
354	                    Some("low") => 1,
355	                    _ => 0,
356	                };
357	                rank(&b.priority).cmp(&rank(&a.priority))
358	            }
359	            TodoSort::CreatedAsc => cmp_opt_str(&a.created_at, &b.created_at, true),
360	            TodoSort::CreatedDesc => cmp_opt_str(&a.created_at, &b.created_at, false),
361	            TodoSort::ModifiedAsc => cmp_opt_str(&a.updated_at, &b.updated_at, true),
362	            TodoSort::ModifiedDesc => cmp_opt_str(&a.updated_at, &b.updated_at, false),
363	        }
364	    }
365	}
366	
367	/// Compare two `Option<String>` slots. `Some` always orders before `None`
368	/// (data first, missing data sinks to the end) regardless of direction; the
369	/// `ascending` flag only affects the `Some`/`Some` case.
370	fn cmp_opt_str(a: &Option<String>, b: &Option<String>, ascending: bool) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
371	    use std::cmp::Ordering;
372	    match (a, b) {
373	        (Some(x), Some(y)) => {
374	            if ascending {
375	                x.cmp(y)
376	            } else {
377	                y.cmp(x)
378	            }
379	        }
380	        (Some(_), None) => Ordering::Less,
381	        (None, Some(_)) => Ordering::Greater,
382	        (None, None) => Ordering::Equal,
383	    }
384	}

386	/// Every [`TodoSort`] variant in cycle order, used by the `s` / `S` and
387	/// `d` / `D` keys and by [`TodoSort::parse`].
388	const ALL_SORTS: [TodoSort; 5] = [
389	    TodoSort::PriorityDesc,
390	    TodoSort::CreatedAsc,
391	    TodoSort::CreatedDesc,
392	    TodoSort::ModifiedAsc,
393	    TodoSort::ModifiedDesc,
394	];

396	/// Run the viewer. `slot` is the routing token the plugin assigned this pane;
397	/// `kind`/`id` are the initial item. The MCP URL is built from `ws` + `port`
398	/// so the form modes can call the daemon.
399	pub fn run(
400	    ws: Option<PathBuf>,
401	    port: u16,
402	    slot: String,
403	    kind: Option<String>,
404	    id: Option<u64>,
405	) -> Result<()> {
406	    let ws = crate::todo::resolve_ws(ws)?;
407	    // Build the observer URL up front; every form load reuses it. An observer
408	    // connection cannot acquire locks, which is fine for this pass - the
409	    // form only displays `locked_by` from todo_get and does not call
410	    // todo_lock. Active lock acquisition is a follow-up.
411	    let url = observer_url(Some(ws.clone()), port)?;
412	    let target = kind
413	        .as_deref()
414	        .and_then(|k| Target::parse(k, id))
415	        .unwrap_or(Target::Empty);
416	
417	    let mut viewer = Viewer::new(ws, url, &slot, target);
418	    let mut terminal = ratatui::init();
419	    // Bracketed paste turns a clipboard paste into a single `Event::Paste(s)`
420	    // instead of a stream of synthetic key events. Without this, multi-line
421	    // pastes arrive as a series of `Ctrl-J` events (the raw `\n` byte in raw
422	    // mode), which `tui_textarea` interprets as `delete_line_by_head` - the
423	    // pasted text scrubs itself across the field as each line break fires the
424	    // shortcut. Failing to enable is non-fatal: typed input still works.
425	    // Mouse capture lets the viewer receive clicks on list rows so the user
426	    // can open todos and notes by clicking, matching the sidebar's
427	    // click-to-activate behaviour. Failing to enable is non-fatal: keyboard
428	    // navigation still works.
429	    let _ = execute!(stdout(), EnableBracketedPaste, EnableMouseCapture);
430	    let outcome = viewer.event_loop(&mut terminal);
431	    let _ = execute!(stdout(), DisableBracketedPaste, DisableMouseCapture);
432	    ratatui::restore();
433	
434	    // The viewer is long-lived, but an explicit close is the user closing it;
435	    // close the Zellij pane too so it does not linger as a spent command pane.
436	    if std::env::var_os("ZELLIJ").is_some() {
437	        let _ = std::process::Command::new("zellij")
438	            .args(["action", "close-pane"])
439	            .status();
440	    }
441	    outcome
442	}

444	/// The running state of a viewer pane.

535	    /// Draw, wait briefly for input, poll for re-points and content changes,
536	    /// flush any pending autosave; repeat until the user closes the pane.
537	    fn event_loop(&mut self, terminal: &mut DefaultTerminal) -> Result<()> {
538	        loop {
539	            if self.needs_draw {
540	                terminal.draw(|frame| self.draw(frame))?;
541	                self.needs_draw = false;
542	            }
543	            if event::poll(TICK).context("polling for input")? {
544	                match event::read().context("reading an input event")? {
545	                    Event::Key(key) if key.kind == KeyEventKind::Press && self.handle_key(key) => {
546	                        return Ok(());
547	                    }
548	                    Event::Paste(s) => self.handle_paste(&s),
549	                    Event::Mouse(m) => self.handle_mouse(m),
550	                    Event::Resize(_, _) => self.needs_draw = true,
551	                    _ => {}
552	                }
553	            }
554	            self.poll_routing();
555	            self.maybe_refresh();
556	            self.maybe_autosave();
557	            self.refresh_sole_content();
558	        }
559	    }
560	
561	    /// Re-read the gatekeeper's published right-side pane count and cache
562	    /// whether this viewer is now the only one left. Only meaningful inside
563	    /// the cockpit: a stand-alone `panopt _viewer` runs outside Zellij with no
564	    /// gatekeeper publishing the count, so it must always stay closable.
565	    fn refresh_sole_content(&mut self) {
566	        self.sole_content_pane = std::env::var_os("ZELLIJ").is_some()
567	            && read_content_count(&self.ws).is_some_and(|n| n <= 1);
568	    }
569	
570	    /// Handle one key press; return `true` to quit. In form mode the form
571	    /// handles most keys; Ctrl-C is reserved as the close gesture so it does
572	    /// not collide with typed input.
573	    fn handle_key(&mut self, key: KeyEvent) -> bool {
574	        let ctrl = key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL);
575	        // Each arm yields `true` to mean "the user asked to close". The actual
576	        // close is deferred to `close_gesture` after the match so it runs once
577	        // the `&mut self.content` borrow the form arms hold has been released.
578	        let close = match &mut self.content {
579	            Content::TodoForm(form) => {
580	                if ctrl && matches!(key.code, KeyCode::Char('c')) {
581	                    // Flush any unsaved edits before the pane goes away.
582	                    let _ = form.flush();
583	                    true
584	                } else {
585	                    match form.handle_key(key) {
586	                        crate::todo_form::TodoFormAction::Close => {
587	                            let _ = form.flush();
588	                            true
589	                        }
590	                        crate::todo_form::TodoFormAction::Dirty
591	                        | crate::todo_form::TodoFormAction::Idle => {
592	                            self.needs_draw = true;
593	                            false
594	                        }
595	                    }
596	                }
597	            }
598	            Content::NoteForm(form) => {
599	                if ctrl && matches!(key.code, KeyCode::Char('c')) {
600	                    let _ = form.flush();
601	                    true
602	                } else {
603	                    match form.handle_key(key) {
604	                        crate::note_form::NoteFormAction::Close => {
605	                            let _ = form.flush();
606	                            true
607	                        }
608	                        crate::note_form::NoteFormAction::Dirty
609	                        | crate::note_form::NoteFormAction::Idle => {
610	                            self.needs_draw = true;
611	                            false
612	                        }
613	                    }
614	                }
615	            }
616	            _ => {
617	                match key.code {
618	                    KeyCode::Char('c') if ctrl => return self.close_gesture(),
619	                    // `q` closes only outside the form; in form mode the user
620	                    // can type a `q` into the title.
621	                    KeyCode::Char('q') => return self.close_gesture(),
622	                    KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Char('k') => self.move_by(-1),
623	                    KeyCode::Down | KeyCode::Char('j') => self.move_by(1),
624	                    KeyCode::PageUp => self.move_by(-(self.viewport.max(1) as i64)),
625	                    KeyCode::PageDown => self.move_by(self.viewport.max(1) as i64),
626	                    KeyCode::Home | KeyCode::Char('g') => self.move_by(i64::MIN / 2),
627	                    KeyCode::End | KeyCode::Char('G') => self.move_by(i64::MAX / 2),
628	                    KeyCode::Enter => self.open_selected(),
629	                    // Status filter for the todo list. Lowercase `f` cycles
630	                    // forward, capital `F` cycles back; both are no-ops for
631	                    // other targets so the binding does not collide there.
632	                    KeyCode::Char('f') => self.cycle_filter(true),
633	                    KeyCode::Char('F') => self.cycle_filter(false),
634	                    // Two-level sort: `s`/`S` cycles level 1, `d`/`D` cycles
635	                    // level 2. Same target-scoping as the filter keys above.
636	                    KeyCode::Char('s') => self.cycle_sort(1, true),
637	                    KeyCode::Char('S') => self.cycle_sort(1, false),
638	                    KeyCode::Char('d') => self.cycle_sort(2, true),
639	                    KeyCode::Char('D') => self.cycle_sort(2, false),
640	                    _ => return false,
641	                }
642	                self.needs_draw = true;
643	                false
644	            }
645	        };
646	        if close {
647	            self.close_gesture()
648	        } else {
649	            false
650	        }

729	    /// The filtered list cursor's position in terminal row `row`, or `None`
730	    /// when the row falls on the header, the footer, or past the last visible
731	    /// entry. The body always starts at row 1 (right after the 1-row header)
732	    /// and is `viewport` rows tall.
733	    fn list_row_at(&self, row: u16) -> Option<usize> {
734	        if !matches!(self.content, Content::List(_)) {
735	            return None;
736	        }
737	        if row == 0 || row > self.viewport {
738	            return None;
739	        }
740	        let visible_len = self.visible_indices().len();
741	        let body_row = (row - 1) as usize;
742	        let start = list_scroll(self.cursor, self.viewport as usize, visible_len);
743	        let idx = start + body_row;

747	    /// Move the cursor (list mode) or the scroll offset (document mode) by
748	    /// `delta` rows, clamped to the content. The list cursor is in *visible*
749	    /// space - it skips entries the filter hides.
750	    fn move_by(&mut self, delta: i64) {
751	        match &self.content {
752	            Content::List(_) => {
753	                let max = self.visible_indices().len().saturating_sub(1) as i64;
754	                self.cursor = (self.cursor as i64 + delta).clamp(0, max.max(0)) as usize;
755	            }
756	            Content::Doc(lines) => {
757	                let max = (lines.len() as i64 - self.viewport as i64).max(0);
758	                self.scroll = (self.scroll as i64 + delta).clamp(0, max) as u16;

760	            Content::Message(_) | Content::TodoForm(_) | Content::NoteForm(_) => {}
761	        }

764	    /// In list mode, route the viewer to the selected (visible) item.
765	    fn open_selected(&mut self) {
766	        if let Content::List(entries) = &self.content {
767	            let visible = self.visible_indices();
768	            if let Some(&idx) = visible.get(self.cursor) {
769	                if let Some(entry) = entries.get(idx) {

777	    /// The indices of `Content::List` entries that pass the current filter,
778	    /// in display order. For [`Target::TodoList`] the indices are reordered
779	    /// by [`Self::todo_sort_1`] then [`Self::todo_sort_2`] (a stable sort,
780	    /// so equal level-1 keys keep their level-2 ordering). For other targets
781	    /// the filter is the identity and no sort is applied, so this returns
782	    /// every index in source order.
783	    fn visible_indices(&self) -> Vec<usize> {
784	        let Content::List(entries) = &self.content else {
785	            return Vec::new();
786	        };
787	        let is_todo_list = matches!(self.target, Target::TodoList);
788	        let mut visible: Vec<usize> = entries
789	            .iter()
790	            .enumerate()
791	            .filter_map(|(i, e)| {
792	                if !is_todo_list || self.todo_filter.includes(e) {
793	                    Some(i)
794	                } else {
795	                    None
796	                }
797	            })
798	            .collect();
799	        if is_todo_list {
800	            // Stable sort by level 2 first, then by level 1: ties on level 1
801	            // preserve the level-2 ordering established by the first pass.
802	            visible.sort_by(|&i, &j| self.todo_sort_2.cmp_entries(&entries[i], &entries[j]));
803	            visible.sort_by(|&i, &j| self.todo_sort_1.cmp_entries(&entries[i], &entries[j]));
804	        }
805	        visible
806	    }

808	    /// Cycle the todo filter forward (`f`) or backward (`F`). No-op when the
809	    /// active target isn't the todo list.
810	    fn cycle_filter(&mut self, forward: bool) {
811	        if !matches!(self.target, Target::TodoList) {
812	            return;
813	        }
814	        self.todo_filter = if forward {
815	            self.todo_filter.next()
816	        } else {
817	            self.todo_filter.prev()
818	        };
819	        // The visible-entry set just changed; keep the cursor on the new
820	        // visible range and persist the choice for next time.
821	        let visible_len = self.visible_indices().len();
822	        if self.cursor >= visible_len {
823	            self.cursor = visible_len.saturating_sub(1);
824	        }
825	        self.persist_viewstate();
826	        self.needs_draw = true;
827	    }
828	
829	    /// Cycle one sort level forward or backward. `level` is 1 (`s` / `S`)
830	    /// or 2 (`d` / `D`); any other value is a no-op. No-op when the active
831	    /// target isn't the todo list. Reordering does not change which entries
832	    /// are visible, but the selected row may now point at a different todo;
833	    /// reset the cursor to the top so the user sees the new ordering from
834	    /// its head rather than scrolled into the middle.
835	    fn cycle_sort(&mut self, level: u8, forward: bool) {
836	        if !matches!(self.target, Target::TodoList) {
837	            return;
838	        }
839	        let slot = match level {
840	            1 => &mut self.todo_sort_1,
841	            2 => &mut self.todo_sort_2,
842	            _ => return,
843	        };
844	        *slot = if forward { slot.next() } else { slot.prev() };
845	        self.cursor = 0;
846	        self.persist_viewstate();
847	        self.needs_draw = true;
848	    }

850	    /// Re-point the viewer at `target`, persisting the outgoing item's
851	    /// position, restoring the incoming one's, and flushing the form if we
852	    /// are leaving one.
853	    fn switch(&mut self, target: Target) {
854	        if target == self.target {
855	            return;
856	        }
857	        // Flush a pending form edit before it disappears.
858	        match &mut self.content {
859	            Content::TodoForm(form) => {
860	                let _ = form.flush();
861	            }
862	            Content::NoteForm(form) => {
863	                let _ = form.flush();
864	            }
865	            _ => {}
866	        }
867	        self.persist_viewstate();
868	        self.target = target;
869	        let vs = viewstate::get(&self.ws, &self.target.key());
870	        self.scroll = vs.scroll;
871	        self.cursor = vs.cursor;
872	        self.todo_filter = vs
873	            .extras
874	            .get("todo_filter")
875	            .and_then(Value::as_str)
876	            .map(TodoFilter::parse)
877	            .unwrap_or_default();
878	        self.todo_sort_1 = vs
879	            .extras
880	            .get("todo_sort_1")
881	            .and_then(Value::as_str)
882	            .map(TodoSort::parse)
883	            .unwrap_or(TodoSort::PriorityDesc);
884	        self.todo_sort_2 = vs
885	            .extras
886	            .get("todo_sort_2")
887	            .and_then(Value::as_str)
888	            .map(TodoSort::parse)
889	            .unwrap_or(TodoSort::CreatedAsc);
890	        self.reload_content();
891	        self.needs_draw = true;
892	    }

923	    /// If the routing file changed, switch to the item it now names.
924	    fn poll_routing(&mut self) {
925	        let current = mtime(&self.routing_path);
926	        if current == self.routing_mtime {
927	            return;
928	        }
929	        self.routing_mtime = current;
930	        let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&self.routing_path) else {
931	            return;
932	        };
933	        let Ok(payload) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&text) else {
934	            return;
935	        };
936	        let kind = payload.get("kind").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
937	        let id = payload.get("id").and_then(Value::as_u64);
938	        if let Some(target) = Target::parse(kind, id) {
939	            self.switch(target);
940	        }
941	    }

943	    /// Re-read the content file if it changed since the last read. Projection-
944	    /// backed targets compare mtimes; form-backed targets (which have no
945	    /// projection file) call `refresh_from_daemon` on the form itself, which
946	    /// pulls a fresh `todo_get` snapshot, replays the local Baseline-diff
947	    /// rules to keep pending edits intact, and updates the Baseline so the
948	    /// next [`Self::maybe_autosave`] flushes only what is still divergent.
949	    fn maybe_refresh(&mut self) {
950	        if self.last_refresh.elapsed() < REFRESH {
951	            return;
952	        }
953	        self.last_refresh = Instant::now();
954	        if let Some(path) = self.target.content_path(&self.ws) {
955	            let current = mtime(&path);
956	            if current != self.content_mtime {
957	                self.reload_content();
958	                self.needs_draw = true;
959	            }
960	            return;
961	        }
962	        // No projection file - form targets refresh through the daemon.
963	        match &mut self.content {
964	            Content::TodoForm(form) => match form.refresh_from_daemon() {
965	                Ok(true) => self.needs_draw = true,
966	                Ok(false) => {}
967	                Err(e) => {
968	                    form.message = format!("refresh failed: {e:#}");
969	                    self.needs_draw = true;
970	                }
971	            },
972	            Content::NoteForm(form) => match form.refresh_from_daemon() {
973	                Ok(true) => self.needs_draw = true,
974	                Ok(false) => {}
975	                Err(e) => {
976	                    form.message = format!("refresh failed: {e:#}");
977	                    self.needs_draw = true;
978	                }
979	            },
980	            _ => {}
981	        }
982	    }

984	    /// If a form edit has been pending for at least [`DEBOUNCE`], flush it.
985	    /// Errors are surfaced in the form's message line by the form itself.
986	    fn maybe_autosave(&mut self) {
987	        let promote = match &mut self.content {
988	            Content::TodoForm(form)
989	                if form.dirty_since.is_some_and(|t| t.elapsed() >= DEBOUNCE) =>
990	            {
991	                if let Err(e) = form.flush() {
992	                    form.message = format!("autosave failed: {e:#}");
993	                }
994	                self.needs_draw = true;
995	                promotion_target(&self.target, form.id)
996	            }
997	            Content::NoteForm(form)
998	                if form.dirty_since.is_some_and(|t| t.elapsed() >= DEBOUNCE) =>
999	            {
1000	                if let Err(e) = form.flush() {
1001	                    form.message = format!("autosave failed: {e:#}");
1002	                }
1003	                self.needs_draw = true;
1004	                promotion_target(&self.target, form.id)
1005	            }

1007	        };

1013	    /// Once a new-todo / new-note form's first save assigns an id,
1014	    /// rewrite the routing file so the sidebar plugin re-titles the pane from
1015	    /// "New todo" to "Todo #N - ...". The form content is already in sync with
1016	    /// the daemon's view, so this only updates the pane title surface - no
1017	    /// reload, no switch (which would clobber the form state).
1018	    fn promote_form_target(&mut self, target: Target) {

1020	            Target::Todo(id) => ("todo", *id),
1021	            Target::Note(id) => ("note", *id),

1031	    /// Load the current target's content. For form targets this calls the
1032	    /// daemon (`todo_get`, `note_get`) or constructs a blank form; for
1033	    /// everything else it reads the `.panopt/` projection.

1035	        let path = self.target.content_path(&self.ws);
1036	        self.content_mtime = path.as_deref().and_then(mtime);
1037	        self.content = match &self.target {
1038	            Target::Empty => Content::Message("Select an item in the sidebar.".to_string()),
1039	            Target::NewTodo => Content::TodoForm(Box::new(TodoForm::blank(&self.url))),
1040	            Target::Todo(id) => match load_todo(&self.url, *id) {
1041	                Ok(todo) => {
1042	                    let url = self.url.clone();
1043	                    let blocker_titles = |bid: u64| resolve_blocker_title(&url, bid);
1044	                    match TodoForm::from_todo(&self.url, &todo, &blocker_titles) {
1045	                        Ok(form) => Content::TodoForm(Box::new(form)),
1046	                        Err(e) => Content::Message(format!("could not parse todo #{id}: {e:#}")),
1047	                    }
1048	                }

1050	            },
1051	            Target::NewNote => Content::NoteForm(Box::new(NoteForm::blank(&self.url))),

1055	                        .as_array()
1056	                        .map(|a| {

1059	                                .collect()
1060	                        })
1061	                        .unwrap_or_default();

1063	                        &self.url,
1064	                        *id,
1065	                        pad["title"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
1066	                        pad["body"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
1067	                        &tags,
1068	                        pad["created_at"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),

1071	                }
1072	                Err(e) => Content::Message(format!("could not load note #{id}: {e:#}")),
1073	            },
1074	            Target::TodoList => match load_todo_list(&self.url) {
1075	                Ok(entries) => Content::List(entries),

1108	    fn draw(&mut self, frame: &mut Frame) {
1109	        // Form modes own the entire pane - their draw renders header, fields,
1110	        // sections, and footer themselves. Other modes use the legacy 3-row
1111	        // layout (header / content / footer).
1112	        if let Content::TodoForm(form) = &mut self.content {
1113	            form.draw(frame, frame.area());
1114	            return;
1115	        }
1116	        if let Content::NoteForm(form) = &mut self.content {
1117	            form.draw(frame, frame.area());
1118	            return;
1119	        }
1120	
1121	        let rows = Layout::vertical([
1122	            Constraint::Length(1), // header
1123	            Constraint::Min(0),    // content
1124	            Constraint::Length(1), // footer
1125	        ])
1126	        .split(frame.area());
1127	        self.viewport = rows[1].height;
1128	
1129	        frame.render_widget(
1130	            Paragraph::new(self.header()).style(Style::default().add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)),
1131	            rows[0],
1132	        );
1133	
1134	        self.draw_body(frame, rows[1]);
1135	
1136	        frame.render_widget(
1137	            Paragraph::new(self.footer()).style(Style::default().fg(Color::Yellow)),
1138	            rows[2],
1139	        );
1140	    }

1142	    fn draw_body(&self, frame: &mut Frame, area: Rect) {
1143	        match &self.content {
1144	            Content::Doc(lines) => {
1145	                let text = Text::from(
1146	                    lines
1147	                        .iter()
1148	                        .map(|l| Line::from(l.clone()))
1149	                        .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
1150	                );
1151	                frame.render_widget(
1152	                    Paragraph::new(text)
1153	                        .wrap(Wrap { trim: false })
1154	                        .scroll((self.scroll, 0)),
1155	                    area,
1156	                );
1157	            }
1158	            Content::List(entries) => {
1159	                let visible = self.visible_indices();
1160	                let viewport = self.viewport as usize;
1161	                let start = list_scroll(self.cursor, viewport, visible.len());
1162	                let lines: Vec<Line> = visible
1163	                    .iter()
1164	                    .enumerate()
1165	                    .skip(start)
1166	                    .take(viewport.max(1))
1167	                    .filter_map(|(visible_i, &raw_i)| {
1168	                        let entry = entries.get(raw_i)?;
1169	                        let style = if visible_i == self.cursor {
1170	                            Style::default().add_modifier(Modifier::REVERSED)
1171	                        } else {
1172	                            Style::default()
1173	                        };
1174	                        Some(Line::styled(format!(" {}", entry.label), style))
1175	                    })
1176	                    .collect();
1177	                let body = if visible.is_empty() {
1178	                    Text::from(" (empty)")
1179	                } else {
1180	                    Text::from(lines)
1181	                };
1182	                frame.render_widget(Paragraph::new(body), area);
1183	            }
1184	            Content::Message(msg) => {
1185	                frame.render_widget(
1186	                    Paragraph::new(format!(" {msg}")).style(Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray)),
1187	                    area,
1188	                );
1189	            }
1190	            Content::TodoForm(_) | Content::NoteForm(_) => {

1355	            let created_at = t["created_at"].as_str().map(str::to_string);
1356	            let updated_at = t["updated_at"].as_str().map(str::to_string);

1360	                status: Some(status),

1362	                priority: Some(priority),

1364	                updated_at,

1371	/// `- [#1](note/1.md) the title` - into its id and trailing label.
1372	fn parse_index_line(line: &str) -> Option<(u64, String)> {
1373	    let line = line.trim();
1374	    if !line.starts_with("- [") {
1375	        return None;
1376	    }
1377	    let hash = line.find("[#")? + 2;
1378	    let close = line[hash..].find(']')? + hash;
1379	    let id: u64 = line[hash..close].parse().ok()?;
1380	    let label_at = line[close..].find(") ")? + close + 2;
1381	    let label = line.get(label_at..).unwrap_or("").trim().to_string();
1382	    Some((id, label))
1383	}

**#140 done.** Agent config management UI is built, verified (check + clippy clean, 350 tests green incl. 12 new), and the todo is marked complete.

## What landed

**Full-stack `system_prompt`** (you opted into the migration):
- `db.rs` V14 — forward-only `ALTER TABLE agent_tools ADD COLUMN system_prompt TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` (+ migration test)
- Threaded through `AgentTool`/`AgentToolPatch` model → `state.rs` create/get/list/update SQL → `AgentToolDto` → MCP `AgentToolCreate/UpdateArgs` → handler dispatch → `panopt agent-tool add/set --system-prompt`

**New `agent_config_form.rs`** — the CRUD form, hosted in `_viewer` like the todo/note forms:
- Fields: Name, Display, **Type** (cycling dropdown seeded from `ProfileSet::load()` — can only land on a known profile, so an invalid type can't be submitted), Command, Working dir, **Enabled** toggle, multi-line **System prompt** body
- Autosave on debounce + refresh-while-open with baseline-diff conflict detection (#40/#65 parity); `agent_tool_create` on first save, `agent_tool_update` after

**`viewer.rs`** — `Target::AgentConfig`/`NewAgentConfig`, `Content::AgentConfigForm`, all the reload/draw/key/paste/mouse/refresh/autosave/promotion paths wired.

content.text:
Found it. The root cause: todo/note `n` **reuses** the existing viewer already in the content slot (`viewer_slot_of` matches), so no new pane. But the Agents content slot holds the live **agent pane** (not a viewer), so `ensure_viewer_in_slot` can't reuse it — it swaps the agent out (suppressing it) and on Ctrl-C the slot empties, which trips the Todos **content floor** (`ensure_content_slot`) into spawning replacement empty viewers. That's the cascade.

The clean fix: the config form is a transient editor, so open it as a **floating** pane (like the delete-gate/search dialogs) — floating panes are excluded from the content-slot/floor accounting (`!p.floating`), so they never disturb the agent pane or trip the floor, and they close cleanly. Let me check the floating-spawn helper.

The cascade comes from swapping the live agent pane out of the slot and then the floor refilling it. Floating the form avoids the slot entirely. But the `_viewer` has a `sole_content_pane` close-refusal (so the last *tiled* pane can't be closed) — a floating viewer would wrongly think it's the sole content pane and refuse Ctrl-C. content.text:
Fixed. Artifacts are rebuilt and staged.

## Root cause
The todo/note `n` works because their content slot already holds a viewer, so it just **rewrites that viewer's routing** in place — no new pane. But the Agents content slot holds the **live agent pane**, not a viewer. So `ensure_viewer_in_slot` couldn't reuse it: it swapped the agent out (suppressing it), and on Ctrl-C the slot emptied, which tripped the Todos-gatekeeper **content floor** (`ensure_content_slot`) into spawning replacement empty viewers — the cascade you saw.

## The fix
The config form is a transient editor, so it now opens as a **floating overlay** (`panopt _viewer --transient`), like the delete-gate and search dialogs:
- Floating panes are excluded from the content-slot/floor accounting (`!p.floating`), so the form never disturbs the running agent pane and never trips the floor.
- The agent pane stays put underneath — you edit a running agent's config without hiding it.
- It's the same `_viewer` process, so autosave + refresh-while-open still work.
- New `--transient` flag disables the `_viewer`'s "sole content pane" close-refusal (that refusal protects the last *tiled* pane; a floating pane is never that), so Ctrl-C always closes it cleanly.

Both `n` (new) and `e` (edit) in the Agents pane now route through the floating `spawn_config_form`.

Verified: `just check` + `just clippy` clean (workspace + wasm), panopt tests green (170).

## To pick it up
The plugin wasm and `panopt` binary are rebuilt. From a **plain shell** (not inside Zellij):

```
just refresh
```

That kills the session + daemon and re-ups with the new plugin and the V14-migrated DB. Then: start an agent, go to Agents, `n` → floating new-config form, Ctrl-C closes it with the agent and layout intact.

If you'd rather I drive a live check another way, say so — but `just refresh` has to run outside Zellij, so it's best from your shell.

{"id":135,"title":"EPIC: Agent model — types (profiles) → configs (slots) → instances (runs)","body":"Umbrella for refining the agent model into three explicit levels, converged in design discussion 2026-05-31. Tracks the child todos tagged `agent-model`.

## The three levels

1. **Agent types = data (profiles), not code.** A type is a *profile row* that drives a fixed set of generic interpreters; `tool_type` becomes a key into a profile registry. There is no per-type code in the common case.
   - **Launch is data**: a spawn-spec template — `argv` template + `env` map + `files`-to-materialize — over a fixed placeholder set (`{agent_id, name, token, mcp_url, project_path, cwd, model, …}`). env-vs-flag-vs-config-file are just *where a placeholder lands*, not different mechanisms. One substitution engine, not a branch per type.
   - **Status is data**: pattern rules (`thinking/idle/waiting/done`) over agent output, run by one generic pattern engine.
   - **Irreducibly code** (fixed, generic, never per-type): the interpreters (substitution, pattern, health/pane-death) and the placeholder providers (the code that produces `token`/`mcp_url`/`agent_id`). New per-type code is needed only for a genuinely new *step kind* the interpreters can't express — rare, and reusable as data once added.
   - **Scope**: global, layered — shipped-defaults file ← machine/user overrides. Distinct from per-project `agent_tools`.

2. **Agent configs = per-project durable slots** (`agent_tools`, shipped in #27). Reference a type; hold name, cwd, command/arg overrides, system prompt, `enabled`. A slot is a lifecycle-managed line in the project's agents pane.

3. **Agent instances = per-project ephemeral runs** (`processes`, shipped in #27 with reserved `pid/status/agent_state/last_seen`). Reference a config; one per config (1:1 policy, N:1 door left open). Born on start, die on stop.

## Why config and instance stay separate even at 1:1
They are *desired state vs. running state* (spec/status): config = what you want, instance = what's happening, and they legitimately diverge (edited-but-not-restarted, crashed, never-started). Decisively, run-level identity is needed so **sessions (#113) and plans (#105) attach to a run, not the durable slot**. The 1:1 keeps the *UI* one-row-per-slot regardless.

## Relationship to existing todos
- #27 (config/instance schema split) — **schema + MCP surface shipped**; remaining wiring lives in the `tool_type → profile` child. Recommend verifying and closing #27.
- #83 (declared-identity registry) — the registry is the *runtime presence* of an instance; the liveness child must consume it, not re-model liveness.
- #111 (monitor agent status in pane) — **absorbed** by the lifecycle-UI child.
- #105 (plans), #113 (sessions) — downstream consumers; this work gives them a run to attach to.

## Agent orchestration surface (solo parity) — added 2026-06-06
The model + lifecycle + human-cockpit-UI children leave a gap: the **agent-facing orchestration surface** an orchestrator agent uses to spawn + bootstrap + task + dispose sub-agents (modelled on solo's `spawn_agent`/`send_input`/`close_process`). Two new children, both riding the #141 daemon-decides / plugin-effects seam:
- **#159 — spawn surface**: `spawn_agent` alias over `process_start`; returns rendered `agent_instructions` (per-type profile template, #136/#137); per-launch `name`/`extra_args` that don't mutate the config.
- **#160 — input channel**: `send_input(process_id, input)` enqueued by the daemon, written into the owned pane by the plugin (`write_chars_to_pane_id`). The linchpin that turns a spawned child into a working one with no human keystroke.

Mappings & non-goals:
- solo's `close_process` == panopt's existing `process_stop` (kill process, **pane stands** per the never-close-panes invariant) + `process_delete`. No new tool needed; documented on #141.
- `project_id` cross-project spawn is a **deferred non-goal** — collides with the per-connection `?ws=` project scoping. Revisit when a real cross-project orchestration case appears.

## DESIGN
Split §6.6 into configs/instances + a new §6.7 "Agent type profiles"; promote §10's spawn bullet into a real lifecycle subsection. #140 is done and committed. Here's where the **#135 epic** stands:

**Done:** #136 #137 #138 #139 #140 #141 #142 (the whole types→configs→instances spine + config UI + lifecycle record + liveness).

**Open children (all now unblocked):**

| # | Title | Blockers | Status |
|---|-------|----------|--------|
| **143** | Instance lifecycle UI: start/stop controls + status badges | 141, 142 ✓ | unblocked |
| **159** | Orchestration spawn surface: `spawn_agent` alias + bootstrap instructions + per-launch overrides | 141 ✓ | unblocked |
| **160** | Instance input channel: `send_input` MCP → plugin writes into pane | 141 ✓ | unblocked |

**My recommendation: #143.** It's the direct sequel to what I just shipped — I'm already deep in `agent_config_form.rs` / `viewer.rs` / the plugin's Agents mode and the lifecycle record landed in #141/#142, so the start/stop controls + status badges are the human-cockpit payoff sitting right on top of plumbing that's fresh in context. It closes out the *human* side of the epic.

#159 and #160 are the **agent-facing orchestration** pair — they ride the same daemon-decides/plugin-effects seam (#141) but serve an orchestrator agent spawning sub-agents, not the human cockpit. They're a natural unit to do together afterward (#160's `send_input` is what makes #159's spawned child actually do work).

One caveat: the floating-form fix + V14 migration from #140 are built on disk but **not yet loaded** — a `just refresh` (from a plain shell, outside Zellij) is needed to pick them up, and that restarts your session. Worth doing before I start #143 so I'm building on a verified-live base.

Want me to start **#143**?

368	/// A parsed `.panopt/processes.md` line. The line format is preserved from
369	/// the pre-V6 `roster.md` so the existing `[kind] #id label` parser still
370	/// works; any trailing `(from #N)` is dropped from `label` and any trailing
371	/// ` · <status>` (todo #141) is lifted into `status`.
372	pub struct ProcessRow {
373	    pub kind: String,
374	    pub id: u64,
375	    pub label: String,
376	    /// Lifecycle status (`starting`/`running`/`stopped`/...), or `None` for a
377	    /// row that predates lifecycle ownership. Drives the cockpit's reconcile of
378	    /// a `starting` row into a pane.
379	    pub status: Option<String>,
380	    /// The agent type key (`type:<tool_type>` segment, todo #142), present only
381	    /// for agent rows backed by a config. Tells the status reconciler which
382	    /// profile's patterns to classify this instance's output with.
383	    pub tool_type: Option<String>,
384	    /// The last classified activity (`state:<agent_state>` segment, todo #142):
385	    /// `thinking`/`idle`/`waiting`/`done`. `None` until first observed.
386	    pub agent_state: Option<String>,
387	    /// The instance's stable agent id (`agent:<name>` segment, todo #142) - the
388	    /// process row's `name`, which is also the `--id` every agent stamps onto
389	    /// its `panopt _mcp-proxy`/`_agent` invocation. This is the join key the
390	    /// status observer uses to bind a pane to its row: the pane command Zellij
391	    /// surfaces is unreliable (it often reports the agent's `_mcp-proxy` child,
392	    /// not the `_process-run` shim), but that child still carries `--id <name>`,
393	    /// so matching it against this field finds the pane regardless. `None` for
394	    /// rows with no name (command/terminal kinds, migrated rows).
395	    pub agent_id: Option<String>,
396	    /// The backing agent config id, lifted from the ` (from #N)` suffix
397	    /// `render_processes_md` writes for instances spawned from a config. This is
398	    /// the join key the Agents pane uses to bind a config to its single live
399	    /// instance (the 1:1 policy). `None` for command/terminal rows and any
400	    /// instance with no backing config.
401	    pub agent_tool_id: Option<u64>,
402	}
403	
404	/// A parsed `.panopt/agent_tools.md` line: one durable agent config (the
405	/// config layer of the two-layer model). The Agents pane is config-centric -
406	/// each config *is* an agent, with at most one live instance - so this is the
407	/// row it renders, joined to a live [`ProcessRow`] by `id == agent_tool_id`.
408	/// Line format (see `render_agent_tools_md`): `- #<id> <label> [<flag>]<cmd>`.
409	pub struct ConfigRow {
410	    pub id: u64,
411	    pub label: String,
412	    /// Whether the config is offered for spawning (`[enabled]` vs `[disabled]`).
413	    pub enabled: bool,
414	}
415	
416	/// Parse one `.panopt/agent_tools.md` config line into a [`ConfigRow`], or
417	/// `None` for the header / `_(no agent tools)_` placeholder / any malformed
418	/// line. The label runs up to the ` [<flag>]` segment; a trailing command (when
419	/// the config carries one) is ignored - the pane shows the agent, not its argv.
420	pub fn parse_config_line(line: &str) -> Option<ConfigRow> {
421	    let rest = line.trim().strip_prefix("- #")?;
422	    let space = rest.find(' ')?;
423	    let id: u64 = rest[..space].parse().ok()?;
424	    let after = &rest[space + 1..];
425	    let bracket = after.find(" [")?;
426	    let label = after[..bracket].trim().to_string();
427	    let flag_rest = &after[bracket + 2..];
428	    let close = flag_rest.find(']')?;
429	    let enabled = &flag_rest[..close] == "enabled";
430	    Some(ConfigRow { id, label, enabled })
431	}

content.text:
#143 is done and marked complete (and #111 closed as absorbed).

## What I found vs. what I built

Most of the lifecycle UI had already landed incrementally in #141/#142 — start/focus (`Enter`/`u` → `process start`), stop (`d` → `process stop`), and the ` · <state>` status badge from the liveness observer were all wired. The one genuine gap was the **idle-age annotation**: the daemon already computes and projects `· idle:<age>` while an agent sits idle, but the plugin parsed that segment *past* and dropped it — so a parked agent showed only `· idle` with no duration, missing #143's "stale/`last_seen` annotation… consistent with #83's `(idle X)`" requirement.

## Changes

- **`ProcessRow.idle`** — new field; `parse_process_line` now captures the `idle:` segment instead of discarding it (`panopt-zellij-logic`).
- **`agent_config_label`** — while idle, appends the age: `Mediator · idle 3m`. Moved out of the wasm-only plugin crate into `panopt-zellij-logic` so it's **host-testable** (the plugin's own `#[cfg(test)]` can't run natively — `Exec format error` under wasm32).
- **4 new unit tests** (no-instance → bare name; non-idle → state badge; idle → state + age; pre-observation → lifecycle status).

## Verification
- `panopt-zellij-logic`: 39 tests pass (4 new), clippy clean.
- Plugin wasm: clippy clean, release artifact rebuilt (`just plugin-release`).
- #111 ("monitor agent status in pane") closed as absorbed, with a comment explaining the observer→badge path.

Two files changed (+95/−18), **not yet committed**. The rebuilt plugin wasm is staged on disk — a `just refresh` from a plain shell will load it (restarts your Zellij session).

The epic #135 now has only the orchestration pair left: **#159** (`spawn_agent` surface) and **#160** (`send_input` channel). Want me to commit #143, and/or move on to #159+#160?

{"started":true,"todo":{"assignee":"","blockers":[141],"body":"The spawn half of the **agent-facing orchestration surface** — what an orchestrator agent needs to spawn a sub-agent *and have enough back to bootstrap and task it*. Brings panopt to parity with solo's `spawn_agent`. Sibling of the `send_input` child; both ride the #141 daemon-decides/plugin-effects seam.

## Why this is new
The epic so far builds the model (#136-139), lifecycle (#141-142), and the *human cockpit UI* (#140, #143). None of it is the *programmatic* orchestration surface an agent uses to spawn children. `process_start` today takes only `agent_tool_id` and returns the bare process row — not enough to bootstrap a child.

## Scope
- **`agent_instructions` return (the key piece).** Spawn returns rendered bootstrap text the parent prepends to the child's first prompt (its `process_id`, MCP url/token hints, how to identify in the registry). The text is **per-type, so it is profile data**: add an optional multiline `instructions` template to the #136 profile schema, rendered by the #137 interpreter via the *same* placeholder substitution (existing set + a new `{{process_id}}` provider). No per-type code.
- **Per-launch overrides.** `process_start` gains optional `name` and `extra_args`. `extra_args` are appended to the resolved argv by the #137 interpreter for this launch only — copied into the `processes` row, never mutating the `agent_tools` config (matches §6.6 copy-on-spawn). `name` overrides the row's display name for this instance.
- **`spawn_agent` alias.** Add a friendly `spawn_agent` entry to `TOOL_SURFACE` + handler over the same `process_start` dispatch (solo's `spawn_agent` is sugar over `spawn_process`). Keep `process_start` as the generic. Its return grows from the bare row to `{process_id, name, agent_instructions, ...row}`.

## Touch points
- #136 profile schema: optional `instructions` multiline template (additive; no reopen — shipped TOML gains a field).
- #137 interpreter: render `instructions` as one more templated output; append per-launch `extra_args`; add `{{process_id}}` provider.
- panopt-tool-surface: `ProcessStartArgs` gains optional `name`/`extra_args`; new `spawn_agent` ToolDef; richer return type.
- panoptd handler: `spawn_agent` dispatch arm (alias) + enriched return.

## Acceptance
- `spawn_agent(agent_tool_id=N)` returns `{process_id, name, agent_instructions}`; `agent_instructions` is the rendered profile template with real `process_id`/`mcp_url`/`token` substituted.
- `extra_args` reach the spawned argv without changing the `agent_tools` row; a second `spawn_agent` of the same config with different `extra_args` proves no mutation.
- `name` sets the instance display name without touching the config.
- `process_start` still works as the generic; `spawn_agent` is a thin alias (one dispatch path).

## Non-goals (deferred)
- `project_id` cross-project spawn — collides with the per-connection `?ws=` project scoping; revisit when a real cross-project orchestration case appears.

1256	    /// Start an instance of the agent config `agent_tool_id`: the daemon half
1257	    /// of the lifecycle (todo #141). Writes the desired-state row that a
1258	    /// reconciler (the cockpit plugin) turns into a live pane - the daemon
1259	    /// never spawns the pane itself, so this is pure record-keeping.
1260	    ///
1261	    /// The config must exist and be enabled. The policy is **one live instance
1262	    /// per config**: if a non-deleted instance of this config is already
1263	    /// `starting` or `running`, that row is returned unchanged (a no-op the
1264	    /// caller can treat as "focus the existing one") rather than spawning a
1265	    /// second. Otherwise a fresh row is written in
1266	    /// [`process_status::STARTING`], copying the config's command/cwd/name at
1267	    /// spawn time (copy-on-spawn, DESIGN S6.6) so later edits to the config do
1268	    /// not perturb the running instance.

251	    decl: &str,

257	        if existing == column {
258	            return Ok(());
259	        }
260	    }
261	    drop(rows);
262	    drop(stmt);
263	    conn.execute_batch(&format!("ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {decl};"))
